correctness.rationale: Exact first-root splitting on two ladder boundary shapes yields conditional variance recurrences, a forced scalar generating-function ODE, and the explicit positive integral. The published mean generating function has an entire numerator and factorially small deviations from affine mean; only endpoint split means generate the O(1/k) forcing, so the coefficient is finite and the variance grows linearly. At k=b the first-root means are nonconstant, proving positivity. A priority-influence path bound with factorially decreasing path probability controls the O(1) boundary discrepancy in L2 and transfers the variance slope to the ordinary open ladder. Exact rational distribution enumerations for b=1,2,3 and high-precision second moments match independent calculations; finite checks are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary ladder paper provides a dynamic mean and static complexity but not this variance coefficient. The 2014 two-row full distribution is for nearest-neighbor blockade b=1. General finite-range fluctuation theorems do not compute the b>=2 variance coefficient. Search comparisons are qualified; literature priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: An unindexed higher-blockade two-row RSA variance formula may predate this calculation.
The displayed exact constant is a convergent quadrature rather than a simpler closed form; numerical digits are not a formal interval rounding certificate.
An external expert must independently check the priority-influence boundary coupling and singular coefficient argument.

value.rationale: The exact extensive variance of the actual dynamically jammed count is a natural physically measurable invariant not determined by the previously known mean or static complexity. For b=2 the coefficient 0.026794578708563... and variance-to-mean ratio about 0.0702 quantify strong occupation-number noise suppression. The all-fixed-b positive integral is a reusable benchmark for stochastic lattice deposition, beyond a routine finite table. It does not claim a new CLT.
